name: spec-vs-gate-adapter-ab
description: PRE-REGISTERED 2026-07-30, before any run. The decisive test for the type_contract gate. On channel-filter, adding one rejection clause to the task took the SAME code from 0/3 to 3/3 with the gate off -- suggesting the defect is a specification artifact, not a capability limit. This asks whether that holds on adapter-migration, the fixture the gate was built from and where it has replicated evidence (4/9 armed vs 0/15 off, p=0.012). Three arms, identical repo, starting code and hidden grader: (1) the real under-specified task with the gate off, the 0/15 baseline; (2) the same task with the gate armed, the measured 44% remedy; (3) the task with the rejection clause written into the normalizeTags and normalizeHeaders contracts, gate OFF. PRIMARY METRIC: hidden-contract pass rate. HYPOTHESIS: arm 3 >= arm 2, i.e. writing the requirement is at least as effective as gating for it, and costs no turns. CONSEQUENCE IF CONFIRMED: type_contract should be documented as a fallback for specs you do not control, not as the primary remedy, and the report must say so. FALSIFIED IF: arm 3 does no better than arm 1, which would mean adapter-migration's defect is NOT merely under-specification and the gate is doing independent work.
